short: A pioneering Soviet swept-wing jet fighter that stunned Western forces with its performance during the Korean War.
full:
Introduced in 1949, the Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15 was one of the first successful swept-wing jet fighters. Powered by a reverse-engineered British Rolls-Royce Nene engine, it boasted an exceptional climb rate, heavy armament, and high-altitude performance that initially outclassed United Nations aircraft when it appeared in the Korean War. Its introduction forced the accelerated deployment of the American F-86 Sabre to counter it.

With over 18,000 units built, the MiG-15 remains the most produced jet fighter in aviation history. It was widely exported across the Warsaw Pact and allied nations, forming the backbone of early Cold War Communist air forces. Remarkably, variants of the MiG-15 continue to operate as advanced trainers in the Korean People's Army Air Force into the twenty-first century.
